clue.text: Lie around, say, in underwear

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: to bask is to lie around lazily in the sun

explanation.surface: A lazy figure lounging about in nothing but their underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A basque is a close-fitting bodice worn as lingerie, so it counts as underwear.

clue.text: Note sent over about uncooked meatloaf

indicators.note: about means the turned note goes round the raw meat
sent over in a down clue means the note's letters are flipped to read upwards

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is the written note telling a reader to take heed
uncooked means raw

explanation.surface: A recipe note passed along about serving a meatloaf raw.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sent over' means read upwards; 'about' makes the turned note go round the uncooked meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is a pressed, jellied loaf of meat from a pig's head, a kind of meatloaf.

clue.text: Unions involved in coercion? Just the opposite!

definitions.text: Unions involved in coercion? Just the opposite!

parts.words: Unions involved in coercion? Just the opposite!
parts.note: flip the phrase round: these are marriages where coercion is involved in the union, as when a bride's father forces a wedding at gunpoint

explanation.surface: A remark about trade unions using strong-arm tactics, then a reversal of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unions' looks like trade unions; here they are marriages, and the reversal makes them forced ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurried marriages forced on a couple, traditionally because of a pregnancy, are unions brought about under coercion.

clue.text: One filling seats at university before recital's beginning — English composer's included

indicators.note: included means the composer is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: up means in residence at university
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter of recital is used

parts.note: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: A student at a recital, with an English composer's work on the programme, takes a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is not a placement word here but the archaic synonym; 'included' sets the composer of The Planets inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholsterer pads and covers chairs, literally putting stuffing into seats.

clue.text: Cutting lots of love games, one assumes

definitions.meaning: a cutting of hawthorn or similar planted to grow a hedge

definitions.text: lots of love games, one assumes
definitions.meaning: a tennis set made up of games won to love would be over fast

explanation.surface: A tennis remark: a run of love games would make for a brisk afternoon, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a set of love games is a set that finishes quickly; 'Cutting' is the gardening sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickset means hawthorn slips set in the ground to grow into a hedge, so a cutting.

clue.text: Terribly insular? They're taking the piss

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word insular is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A jibe at insular folk who mock everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the piss' is British slang for mocking someone; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Urinals are the fixtures in a gents' toilet that receive urine, so they literally take it.

clue.text: Rod and line that's caught

indicators.note: caught here means heard by ear, so the word for line is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: An angler's kit: a rod, and a line on which something has been hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like fishing but means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the tapered stick used to strike balls in snooker or pool, a kind of rod.

clue.text: New partner's child's concealed woman and he's protected by dull composer

indicators.note: concealed means the woman is hidden inside the stepson

parts.note: a new partner's son is one's stepson
hen is informal for a woman

indicators.note: protected by means he sits inside the word for dull

parts.note: dim means dull
he, taken as written

explanation.surface: A blended-family drama: a stepchild hides a woman while a man shelters behind a tedious musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' and 'protected by' are both container signals; 'woman' as hen is Scottish and northern usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The American wrote the music and lyrics for Sweeney Todd and Into the Woods, so a composer.

clue.text: They set a precedent with matches in box? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in at first suggests the matches go inside the box
the opposite turns this round, so the box goes inside the matches instead

parts.note: test matches in cricket, so tests
a box is a case

explanation.surface: A matchbox remark about precedents, then the order reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches in box' suggests matchsticks, but they are cricket test matches; 'Just the opposite' swaps which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal actions whose rulings decide later disputes establish precedents for future judgments.

clue.text: Make a fuss when drug is found in old car

indicators.note: is found in means the drug goes inside the car

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, battered car
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Uproar when narcotics are discovered in a battered vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: to create is to throw a tantrum or kick up a row.

clue.text: Hardy's description of inferno heat possibly

parts.note: read as wordplay, the phrase's last word is an anagram signal and its first eleven letters, jumbled, spell these two words; 'possibly' flags the trick

explanation.surface: A writer named Hardy depicting the fires of hell.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy, not Thomas; read as an instruction, the phrase's opening words in a mess give 'inferno heat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The film comedian's catchphrase for the chaos his partner landed them in is exactly this phrase.

clue.text: Politician producing nothing, absolutely nothing, but anger touring outskirts of Goole

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the outer letters of Goole sit inside

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: outskirts means just the outside letters of the town's name

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, slang for absolutely nothing
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A dig at a politician who achieves nothing but stir up fury around a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Goole is a town in East Yorkshire; 'touring' is the container signal, and sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reform UK leader and former UKIP head is a well-known British party politician.

clue.text: Sparks flying in tea circle

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scatter and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Sparks shooting out amid a circle of tea drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparks' looks like a plural noun, but it is the British nickname for the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is the traditional slang nickname for a tradesperson who wires buildings.

clue.text: Hotel 99 here in Rome

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
IC is 99 in loose Roman numerals, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: Hotel number 99 here in the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin adverb meaning 'here', as spoken in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Pietersen's out? A growing concern, perhaps

indicators.note: out suggests the batsman's name is knocked out of its order

parts.note: the England batsman Kevin Pietersen's surname supplies the letters; the possessive adds none

explanation.surface: Kevin Pietersen, the England batsman, has been dismissed: a matter of growing worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A growing concern' is a business that is thriving; here it is something literally growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Conifers are living, growing things, so a forest of them is literally a growing concern.

clue.text: Brief communications containing job and employee's documents

parts.note: a post is a job
an employee's cards are the papers held by an employer, as in 'get your cards'

explanation.surface: Short memos that hold a job offer and the worker's paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, being given your cards means being dismissed, from the National Insurance cards an employer held.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture messages sent through the mail carry only a few lines, so they are short notes.

clue.text: Poster girl somewhere in Ireland

definitions.meaning: Jessica ...-Hill, the heptathlete, was the face of the London 2012 Olympics
the county town of Clare in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A pin-up model found in an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: The British heptathlete was the poster image of London 2012, and the same name is a town in County Clare.

clue.text: Two queens in transparent fabric

parts.note: She, Haggard's 'She who must be obeyed', is an African queen
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the British queen

explanation.surface: A pair of monarchs dressed in see-through cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer describes very fine, see-through material such as chiffon or stockings.

clue.text: One cricketer among rugby tour group drinks

indicators.note: among means the other pieces sit within the touring side

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions are the touring rugby union side
I is the Roman numeral one
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A lone cricketer joins a rugby squad on tour for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Libations are drinks, originally liquids poured out as offerings, now jokingly any alcohol.

clue.text: Delivery method that's on message, according to PR person

parts.note: on and leg are both names for the same side of a cricket field
spin is the slant a PR person puts on a message

explanation.surface: A PR adviser judges a delivery approach to be on message.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side; a bowler's delivery uses wrist spin.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of wrist-spin bowling is a way of delivering the cricket ball.

clue.text: One in order's not right, dash it!

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a brother is a member of a religious order

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that someone's paperwork is not in proper order.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance, like 'blast it!'

clue.text: Hoax method of payment

definitions.meaning: ... is British slang meaning fake or mock, as in a ... accent
..., cash on delivery, means paying when goods arrive

explanation.surface: A scam involving how a bill is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sham in British slang, and the initials stand for cash on delivery.

clue.text: 11's lot cared about having sound principles

parts.note: the politician at 11 across belongs to the political right
minded means cared about, as in 'I wouldn't have minded'

explanation.surface: A politician's followers are concerned with acting on firm values.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of decent views and sound judgement holds honest, sensible principles.

clue.text: Fruit becomes less fresh

definitions.meaning: the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree
something that becomes old-fashioned with time is said to age or go out of style

explanation.surface: Produce that is going stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm fruit, and a verb meaning grows old-fashioned with the passing years.

clue.text: Seek office relocation for printer founders

indicators.note: relocation suggests the letters move to new places

explanation.surface: Firms that build printers need a new office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seek office' looks like house-hunting, but it is about elections.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand for the top elected post is to try to win high office.

clue.text: Famous Jedi's beginning and ending with charm

definitions.meaning: the first part of the Star Wars Jedi master's name
..., or obeah, is a Caribbean charm or fetish

explanation.surface: A Star Wars hero starts and finishes on charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jedi's first name starts with it, and in West Indian folk magic it is a charm.

clue.text: Comedian making unusual noises during Sunday School

indicators.note: during means the jumbled letters sit within the abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for Sunday School

indicators.note: unusual means the word noises comes out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A comic disrupting a church class with strange sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles the noises and 'during' places them within the Sunday School abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: John Sessions was a British comic actor known for improvisation and impressions.

clue.text: Ill feeling one's encountered in back passage

indicators.note: encountered in means the contraction is met inside the passage

parts.note: a coy euphemism for the anus
one's read as 'one is' becomes I'm

explanation.surface: Someone meeting bad vibes in an alley behind the houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' must be expanded to 'one is' and contracted again; 'encountered in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus means hostility or antagonism, a feeling of ill will towards someone.
